transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-16 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 mins | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM); Aisha (GreenCrest Head ML), Marcus (Platform), Ravi (Procurement), Leah (SRE)

Summary: quick renewal + capacity readout for GreenCrest — discuss committed retainer uplift, add EU + Japan nodes, private VPC options, KMS/SSO gating, and next steps for pilot benchmarks. Some audio dropouts and a few transcription errors (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of Redwood Dedicated).

Topics: Retainer uplift math, burst credits, region activation sequence (eu -> japan -> apac), latency SLO targets, security paperwork, procurement timeline, demo/pilot runway.

Action items (captured in metadata above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining; quick roll call — we got Samira, Diego, Priya from Redwood, and Aisha, Marcus, Ravi, Leah from GreenCrest. how's your morning?
[00:26] Aisha: morning all — good, hope so. quick note, we've got our Q2 budget snapshot so we can talk numbers today.
[00:40] Diego: awesome. i'll try to keep the deep tech bits concise but also leave time for the perf questions.
[01:05] Marcus: yeah we care about tail lat as much as cost — last month we saw p95 at about 480ms on our current self-hosted cluster with KV cache disabled under heavy load.
[01:28] Priya: useful context — our goal is to hit p95 < 250ms for customer-facing inference and keep per-token costs under the threshold you shared earlier.
[01:45] Samira: perfect, ok so first item — commitment uplift. we proposed a 3-tier retainer: baseline reserved capacity plus monthly burst credits. this would give you predictable throughput and cheaper unit economics.
[02:10] Ravi: on procurement side, timeline is important — we need contract amendment in place by end of month to align with our finance cycle. is that realistic?
[02:30] Samira: yeah we can, depends on legal review speed; we'll send the amendment draft the week after next, Priya will own coordination.
[03:00] Leah: technical question — for eu and japan nodes, are we looking at Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated in shared infra? data residency is a big ask.
[03:20] Diego: good one — we can do Dedicated (reserved GPUs in our cloud pool) for predictable throughput and Redwood Privatee for customer-managed VPC/on-prem if you need full network control. sorry that got munged in the auto transcript.
[03:45] Aisha: we'd prefer VPC in EU for residency, but for Japan we can tolerate Dedicated until we commit to onprem.
[04:10] Marcus: also need to confirm KMS integration — we use HashiCorp Vault. do you have an HSM/KMS workflow?
[04:30] Diego: yes, we support KMS integrations; we have an ops doc (link) and we've done Vault+HSM for other customers. i'll share the network diagram and KMS checklist after the call.
[04:55] Aisha: great. on perf: we ran a small eval with an open model and saw steady state token throughput at ~600 tps but not the KV cache patterns we expect in prod. can Redwood's runtime do prefix caching?
[05:20] Diego: absolutely — our runtime supports prefix/KV cache and automatic caching policies; in practice that reduces tokens served by up to 30% for chat-heavy workloads. depends on prompt locality.
[05:45] Samira: okay, so proposed activation sequence: 1) provision EU VPC nodes (staging), 2) run internal perf dry-run with your traffic sim, 3) switch prod traffic + enable burst if needed, 4) then roll out Japan Dedicated nodes. Does that match your ops plan?
[06:15] Aisha: yes, that's our preferred path. how long to provision EU VPC?
[06:30] Priya: typically 7-10 business days to stage, less if we get network peering details and KMS creds early.
[06:45] Marcus: peering has to route through our transit gateway; i'll flag potential MTU issues.
[07:05] Diego: noted — we'll run the checklist and surface any routing caveats.
[07:30] Ravi: pricing — can you show the delta if we go from current retainer 100k tokens/mo to 400k tokens/mo plus 200k burst credits?
[07:50] Samira: yes, we'll update the quote; quick ballpark on-call now: unit price drops ~28% with that uplift; I'll send a line-item table.
[08:15] Aisha: also, SLA — do you offer latency SLAs or just uptime? we need some guarantee on response times for high-value flows.
[08:32] Samira: currently our SLA covers availability and throughput targets for Dedicated customers; latency SLAs are possible in enterprise addendum — we can work a targeted p95 SLA into the contract if we validate via perf runs.
[09:00] Leah: ok, for the perf validation can Redwood run a benchmark using our scenario? we can provide scripts.
[09:20] Diego: yes we'll run the benchmark. typical approach: you provide a traffic profile and representative prompts, we run staged tests in EU VPC and capture p50/p95/p99 and cost metrics.
[09:45] Aisha: good. timeline — if we get the network and KMS details by Monday, could you stage EU by next Friday?
[10:05] Priya: probably; Diego and infra will triage immediately. staging Friday is tight but feasible.
[10:24] Marcus: one more on fallback: if EU capacity saturated, can traffic failover to US region? we need cross-region fallback with GDPR considerations.
[10:42] Diego: yes, we can route by policy; however, fallback may require data handling exceptions — we'll need a legal/ops signoff for cross-region processing.
[11:05] Aisha: that'll go to legal; Ravi will coordinate on that.
[11:20] Ravi: noted. any competitor items we should be aware of? we've been talking to LargeCloudAI about an edge option.
[11:34] Samira: understood. our differentiator is the unified runtime + cost controls; we'll share concrete benchmark comparisons if helpful.
[11:55] Aisha: for Japan node sizing, we estimate 30% of EU steady state; we'll confirm numbers.
[12:10] Diego: perfect — we'll propose a small cluster (2-4 GPUs) for Japan Dedicated initially and scale after validation.
[12:30] Priya: logging and observability — you wanted token-level cost breakdowns?
[12:45] Marcus: yes, and trace ids so we can correlate latencies with requests.
[13:00] Diego: we expose per-route dashboards, trace hooks and token cost breakdown in the console; some extra retention is an add-on.
[13:20] Aisha: about audit logs and compliance — SOC2 plus retention windows are must-haves.
[13:34] Samira: we have SOC2 docs and a compliance pack; Diego will attach the network diagrams and the data flow audit doc.
[14:00] Leah: any thought on quantization? we saw cost improvements from 8-bit quant on some open models, are there recommendations?
[14:18] Diego: yes, we have quantization profiles that target throughput vs quality; Redwood Optimize can recommend profiles per model — we'll include suggested configs in the benchmark results.
[14:40] Aisha: excellent. procurement question: if we change to a 12-month amendment with upfront commit, can you offer a stepped discount or credits?
[14:58] Samira: yes — standard: higher commit gives 10-18% off unit price and additional burst credits; I'll model a couple scenarios.
[15:20] Ravi: legal review window: 10 business days typically; we want the commercial terms locked to start that clock.
[15:35] Samira: we'll send commercial terms first.
[16:00] Marcus: on the pilot day, can we run a long-tail stress test that simulates peak campaigns — like a 20-minute surge?
[16:20] Diego: absolutely — we'll coordinate a schedule and run surge plus KV cache hot-warm patterns.
[16:45] Aisha: question — for private deploy, is there an air-gapped onprem option? some workloads need that later.
[17:00] Diego: yes, we offer a private onprem package; it's more involved (ops install + support retainer). we'll outline differences in the doc.
[17:24] Priya: to recap: Redwood to send pricing scenarios/quote, SOC2/compliance pack, network diagrams, and a proposed pilot schedule. GreenCrest to provide traffic profile, KMS access design notes, and procurement timeline.
[17:45] Aisha: yep. one ask — can you put the quote in a way that shows daily cost at 200 req/s and 600 req/s? that's easiest for finance.
[18:05] Samira: yes will do.
[18:20] (brief cross-talk as folks check calendars)
[19:00] Diego: any lingering technical risks? I'm tracking peering MTU, KMS handshake, and fallback policy config.
[19:18] Leah: plus dependency on our transit gateway team — they need heads-up.
[19:34] Marcus: i'll loop them in once Diego sends the diagram.
[20:00] Aisha: ok let's lock tentative dates — pilot dry-run week of 2026-04-26, production cutover week of 2026-05-10 if all goes well.
[20:25] Priya: noted — I'll propose two slots for the dry-run.
[20:40] Samira: perfect. final recap and next steps — Samira to update quote (due 4/19), Diego to share ops docs and KMS checklist (4/20), Priya to coordinate pilot slots (4/22), Marcus to provision network details (4/18), Ravi to start legal review (target 4/29).
[21:10] Aisha: thanks, all. appreciate the clear path.
[21:20] Samira: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the email and attachments.
[21:35] (meeting ends)
